scientific_interpretation.primary: The held-out matrix independently reproduces the hydraulic-state dependence seen in the owner calibration context. Across the tested small prescribed-head jump range, the refinement level at which the raw head defect becomes persistently conservative is controlled much more strongly by hydraulic state than by jump sign or amplitude.
scientific_interpretation.boundedness: A bounded fixed-horizon refinement entry exists for every frozen held-out case, with maximum observed entry N=16 over h0 from -40 to -320 cm.
scientific_interpretation.not_a_universal_error_factor: The defect-to-remaining-error ratio still varies strongly with hydraulic state. Gate A therefore does not admit a universal multiplicative error estimator or a universal absolute production tolerance.
scientific_interpretation.finite_reference_warning: N=512 is a finite reference trajectory, not an exact solution. Ratios near numerical floor are excluded from profile classification.
scientific_interpretation.runtime_semantics_warning: N is the number of equal substeps used to integrate the same 0.25-day fixed horizon. It is not a transaction retry count and cannot be mapped directly to F-KT retries or F-GC02 internal committed substeps.
scientific_interpretation.scope_limit: Evidence applies only to the source-locked homogeneous four-node mode-5 no-optional-physics fixture and tested hydraulic/jump envelope.

next_action: Run a separate production-shape translation gate with unchanged F-GC02 transaction policy. Determine whether the actual retry/substep topology can reach or safely represent the fixed-horizon conservative regime across the held-out hydraulic states without selecting a tolerance or changing production policy.
